name: Momofuku Bossam (Korean Slow-Roasted Pork Shoulder)

gate.notes: 626 cal clears the 650 ceiling and 18g carbs clears the 35g cap on published numbers; optional raw-oyster garnish is dropped for the no-seafood rule; weigh-and-divide roast scales cleanly to 14.

dupe_check.evidence: Not a duplicate of the catalog's Korean pork bowls (slow-cooker-korean-gochujang-pork-bowls, korean-gochujang-ground-pork-rice-bowls, slow-cooker-korean-shredded-pork-bowls), which are all shredded/ground pork over rice in a gochujang braise: bossam differs on 3 of 4 axes (salt+sugar dry cure vs gochujang braise, lettuce-wrap/no-starch vs rice, oven low-and-slow roast + crust vs slow-cook-and-shred). Closest salt-roast concept slow-cooker-kalua-pork-bowls is Hawaiian and a rice bowl, not a Korean lettuce-wrap plate.

cross_protein_watch: The Korean gochujang/ssamjang flavor family is common enough to recur in the beef, chicken, or turkey pools, but bossam's defining format (a salt/sugar dry-cured whole-muscle slow-roast served as lettuce ssam wraps with no starch) is distinctive; watch only for a same-format salt-cured roasted-and-wrapped dish under another protein (e.g. a Korean lettuce-wrap roast beef), which would be a structural twin.
